evals.name: write-new-cli
evals.prompt: Write a concise GitHub README for this project. Help a first-time user understand it and get a useful result. Read the supplied source and project facts. Save README.md and a short validation note under outputs/. Do not invent a published package, URL, or support claim.
evals.expected_output: A complete source-backed introduction and working first-use command with expected output.
expectations: Explains UTF-8 nonempty-line counting, including whitespace-only lines, and read-only behavior.
States Python 3.11+ and direct-checkout use without inventing a package, URL, dependency, or platform guarantee.
Provides a command with directory context that executes against the supplied sample and prints the documented value 2.
Separates commands from output and reports actual validation limits outside the README.

evals.name: assess-existing
evals.prompt: Assess this README for reader usefulness, scannability, slop, and hard-coded cruft. Do not edit the project. Save audit.md under outputs/ with prioritized concerns, evidence status, and material worth preserving.
evals.expected_output: Finds the unsupported command and claims, prioritizes impact, preserves real requirements and collation warning.
expectations: Identifies the unsupported --recursive flag as a confirmed first-use defect and supplies the source-backed correction.
Distinguishes unsupported security/platform/production claims from proven false behavior.
Flags the transient test count and internal phase status without inferring AI authorship.
Prioritizes reader impact and explicitly preserves Python/UTF-8 requirements, Unicode collation caveat, and useful license route.
Leaves all input fixture files unchanged.

evals.name: preserve-working-library
evals.prompt: Polish this README only where it improves the reader experience. Preserve what already works. Save the resulting README.md under outputs/ even if unchanged, plus a brief review.md explaining the decision and checks.
evals.expected_output: A sound README is preserved; any edits retain anchors, constraints, examples, license meaning, and routes.
expectations: Retains the Usage and Limitations anchors, reference link, and license/attribution meaning.
Preserves Python 3.11+, local module use, code-point versus terminal-cell limitations, and whitespace normalization.
Preserves a complete example whose actual output matches the README.
Leaves working content unchanged or explains each edit with a concrete reader benefit; introduces no invented installation or support claims.

evals.name: improve-generated-font
evals.prompt: Improve this font project README for readers choosing and using its assets. Keep the repository publishing workflow working. Copy the fixture into outputs/project/ and make your changes there; save review.md beside the project directory.
evals.expected_output: Removes repetitive promotion while preserving asset routes, format choices, compatibility, split licensing, and generation ownership.
expectations: Edits the owning template and regenerates README so both remain identical.
Preserves specimen and download routes plus the WOFF2 web versus OTF desktop choice.
Preserves variable-font compatibility and static-font fallback without claiming unperformed rendering tests.
Preserves separate font OFL and script MIT licensing and leaves license files unchanged.
Removes repetitive unsupported promotion without inventing package installation or missing font assets.
